claims.text: A controlled sub-glass-transition annealing hold immediately after rapid quenching can improve the glass-forming ability of phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys.
The post-quench sub-Tg annealing hold can enhance the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
Sub-Tg annealing reduces residual free volume in the amorphous alloy.
Sub-Tg annealing relaxes internal stresses in the amorphous alloy.
Residual free volume and internal stresses predispose the metallic glass to crystallization.
A sub-Tg hold permits atomic-scale rearrangements that relieve stress and reduce free volume.
Stress relaxation and free-volume reduction stabilize the amorphous structure against crystallization during subsequent thermal treatment.
The beneficial effect requires the annealing temperature to remain below Tg.
The hold duration must be optimized to permit structural relaxation without triggering crystallization.
Annealing above Tg may cause premature crystallization.
An excessively long annealing hold may cause premature crystallization.
Relative to an otherwise identically quenched unannealed sample, the annealed sample will have a higher DSC crystallization-onset temperature.
A higher crystallization-onset temperature indicates greater resistance to crystallization and increased thermal stability.
